segments.text: Mr.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: President. The senator from Massachusetts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Mr. President, I ask consent that my chief of staff, John Donenberg, be allowed to join me on the floor here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Without objection.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Thank
you, Mr. President.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: Mr.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: President, I rise today to recognize an extraordinary public servant who is leaving my office for a

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: new role.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: John Donnenberg has been one of my most trusted senior advisors since 2011 when I first ran for the United States Senate.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: After his stint advising me on policy during the 2012 campaign, I asked John to serve as my first legislative director in my Senate office. John was my LD for six years, then senior advisor and policy director for Warren for President. And for the last four years, he has served as my Chief
of State.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: After nearly a dozen years of working together, I have come to know John pretty well, so I can say with some authority that he is one of the best policy nerds and sharpest minds on economic policy in the business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: When I arrived in the Senate, I knew more than pretty much anybody else in the world about a very specific slice of commercial law. I also had spent a lot of time thinking about how middle class families were getting crushed by an economy that didn't work for them and thinking through how to fix it. And this was a good start, but being a senator means doing work on a much, much broader range of issues.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: John was the person I turned to for counsel as I developed that broader agenda, drawing on his deep expertise with policy, his facility for digging into data, and his formidable technical training. Also, importantly, John has good values.
The

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: long-standing belief that government is here to serve not the richest and most powerful, not those who can hire armies of lobbyists and lawyers, but here to serve the people who are trying to build a future for themselves and their families. John and I were a good match, and I will say that, when I'm not saying, as part of that, that we always saw our next moves the same way.
But he

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: has a lightning quick mind, a staggering command of both domestic and foreign policy topics and instincts honed by years of working in Congress. And those qualities allowed him to see around corners I didn't even know existed. He's good with numbers and he's never been afraid

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_10
segments.text: to change his mind based on what the data show him. Our relationship has always been energetic.
John

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: hasn't been afraid to tangle with me when he thought I was getting something wrong. He would tell me I was making a mistake and I would tell him he didn't know what he was talking about. We would size each other up and I would start lobbing fastballs at him just like I was back in the classroom trying to figure out if a student had done the reading and was on solid ground in their arguments. John of course has always, always done the reading.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: He would grab those fastballs out of the air and zing them back at me with a spin, often highlighting an aspect to the issue I had failed to consider. Sometimes I would try a
new

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: angle, play the devil's advocate to see if he could defend his position, back and forth until I had, often in the space of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: 10 or 15 minutes, pressure tested an argument more thoroughly than seemed possible. Now, I'm not saying John won all those arguments.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_12
segments.text: But I give him a 50/50 lifetime record, which is pretty respectable in my book. And I'd also say
this:

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: 100% of the time, my thinking about an issue got deeper and sharper as a result of running my views through the gauntlet of John's scrutiny.
Given

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: all these attributes, it should come as no surprise that John had a very specialized skill that is rarely employed among adults

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: outside elected office. John was a whiz at debate prep. He has worked with me and several other senators during our races, helping candidates prepare for pre-election debates.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: He put all of us through our paces, forcing us to confront the frustration and the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_16
segments.text: opportunities of butting heads with our opponents and doing it in one-minute chunks. For all of us who

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_17
segments.text: managed to survive those debates far better than we expected, we owe John our thanks.
When he

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: came to work for me, John brought with him years of experience in Congress. Before joining my office, John served as Chief

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_20
segments.text: Counsel to Senator Richard Blumenthal. Before then, he served as Health Law Advisor to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: Representative Henry Waxman on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the House Energy and Commerce Committee. I asked Henry Waxman for a few words about John, and he had this to say:
John

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: started his congressional career

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_20
segments.text: as a precocious young staffer in my office working on the Affordable Care Act. He's leaving Senator Warren's staff
as a

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_20
segments.text: veteran chief of staff with many distinguished legislative accomplishments. What's been constant is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: the gratitude and respect he has earned from everyone who has been lucky enough to work with him along the
way.
John's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: first

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: experience working in Congress has a special resonance for me. John was a legal fellow for Senator Ted Kennedy, the senior senator from Massachusetts who served for 47 years in the seat I
now hold.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: I think Senator Kennedy would be pleased to know that the young man he first brought in for work in the federal legislature ended up contributing so much to this work.
There is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_13
segments.text: one more aspect of John's leadership that I want to make sure to highlight. He is a dedicated mentor

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: who has trained scores of policy staffers in how to make this country work better for families who don't always have someone in government looking out for
them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: Year after year, I have observed as John invests in the staff on my team and throughout government, supporting them,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_24
segments.text: teaching them, and challenging them, and always, always, always making them better at what they do. Congress is a hard place to work in a lot of ways.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_24
segments.text: John often tells me that trying to make change by working in the Senate can feel a lot like running face-first into a brick wall over and over and over again. You have to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_20
segments.text: keep standing up and sprinting back at the wall because even though history suggests you're

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_13
segments.text: going to smack right into it just like last time, the only way you'll ever smash through the bricks is by taking one more run at it.
John is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: the kind of colleague who makes you want to take one more run

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_20
segments.text: at knocking down the wall that has never been knocked down before. The one who will help you dust yourself off and then sprint along beside you.
I've watched as

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: these staffers who John has trained have transformed from eager, gifted beginners into seasoned strategists. John and I have stood proudly side by side

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: as we've seen them leave our office and take their talents to go make change somewhere else. John's commitment to mentorship means that today we have more dedicated public servants

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_13
segments.text: doing top-notch work all around the country and doing it better because of their time learning from
him.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: Now John is the one who is taking his talents to another public service post.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: He is headed to the White House to serve as deputy director of the National Economic Council. I know John will bring with him to this position an abiding commitment to helping working families, as well

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_29
segments.text: as one of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: the best policy brains in the business.
One last note. John is a

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: good man. He is honest. He is principled. He is generous. He is funny. He cares about people.
He

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: loves his family deeply, and he is always there for

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: his friends. He tries

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_24
segments.text: to live his life every day according to deeply held moral values. I admire
him.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_10
segments.text: So, John, I am grateful down to my toes for the years that we have worked

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: together. I will miss having you by my side, but I know that the president
The

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: nation and the world will be better off because of the challenges you will help tackle in this new role.
Thank you

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: for

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_33
segments.text: your work, both past and present and future. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. I yield the floor.
